Not blocked by a hard wall — recorded as covered-by-proxy, not parked.
- **NEW-RC-10 found + fixed + headless-proven this session (2026-07-18) — the specific bug Michael reported and reproduced live 3× (project "ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST 2026...", a Building element, Properties → Fill opacity slider):** select an element, drag its Fill-opacity slider, then press Ctrl+Z **WITHOUT deselecting or clicking away first** → silently no-op'd. Root cause: the global keydown guard (`SitePlanner.jsx`) treated ANY focused `<input>` — including a `type="range"` slider, which has no native browser undo to protect — as "typing" and unconditionally swallowed Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y before they ever reached the app's undo dispatch. The toolbar Undo button and a click-away-then-Ctrl+Z both already worked (bypassing the guard), and the reverted value already persisted correctly across a reload once undone — so this was purely a keyboard-dispatch gap, not a persistence bug. **Fix:** the guard now lets ONLY the Ctrl/Cmd+Z / +Y chord through when focus is on a range/slider input; every other shortcut (arrows, Delete, letter tools) still respects the guard while a slider has focus, since those DO have real native slider behavior or would nudge/delete the still-selected element out from under the user. **Verified:** full unit suite green (4522) · lint 0 errors · build green · new describe block in `e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js` (2 tests, LOGGED-OUT, green in headless Chromium): (a) drag a Building's Fill-opacity slider then Ctrl+Z with focus still on the slider now correctly reverts it (proven via the persisted model value, since — matching the toolbar Undo button's own documented behavior — the app's `applySnapshot` deselects/closes the Properties panel as part of any undo/redo) and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it; (b) a no-regression check confirms Ctrl+Z with focus in a REAL text field (a callout's inline `<textarea>`, whose placement is already on the undo stack) still does **NOT** fire app undo — proving the fix is scoped to sliders only, not a blanket "any focused input" exception. Sanity-checked the test itself: reverted the guard fix, rebuilt, reran — test (a) failed exactly as expected (value stuck at the dragged-to value); re-applied the fix, reran green — confirms the test genuinely catches the regression rather than being a false positive.
- **Blocker: auth** — the residual pending work is **2** (cloud/idb-backed aerial remove→undo→reload survival, untouched by this session) and the **persistence-only** half of **3** (does the reverted opacity value survive a reload for a signed-in, cloud-synced user — the reversion mechanism itself is now proven, only the reload round-trip needs a live signed-in check); the sandbox egress proxy CORS-blocks the Supabase auth handshake, so sign-in can't run here.

### V197 — B625 (×2): an uploaded metes-and-bounds deed snaps onto the real county parcel — confirm the in-app click-through on Michael's actual Grand Port deed + Chambers County parcel ⏳ needs a signed-in browser on planyr.io with the live GIS reachable · **REOPENED 2026-07-10 for the B625×2 recurrence** (the align tool over-rotated deeds grossly, "~45°"; re-fixed — reconfirm it now rotates only the small basis-of-bearings angle, and no longer force-fits a deed to a parcel it isn't on)
- **Added** 2026-07-02 · **Cadence** once (fix acceptance) · **Last checked** 2026-07-10 (recurrence re-fix: lint 0 errors · **3302 tests green** incl. `test/deedAlign.test.js` 13 (3 new) · build green · `MAP.md` regenerated) · **Next check** — on planyr.io, signed in, on the real project (steps 6–7 below).
- **🔁 Recurrence re-fix (2026-07-10, B625×2):** the align feature snapped a plotted deed to a gross rotational alias (tens of degrees, "~45°") instead of the ~1.5° basis-of-bearings correction — because `solveDeedAlignment` searched the full ±180° for the lowest nearest-vertex RMS and a near-symmetric / generalized outline aliased to 45/90/180°, and `bestDeedFit` force-fit a deed to the nearest parcel even when none was under it (the reporter's floating 42-ac tract). **Fixed** by (A) bounding the rotation search to `MAX_ALIGN_ROT_DEG = 20°` in `deedAlign.js` (a >window mismatch is reported not-confident, never force-rotated) and (B) a spatial-correspondence gate in `bestDeedFit` (overlap ≥ ½ the smaller footprint via `polyIntersectArea` + areas within ~4:3) so a non-corresponding parcel can't hijack the fit → it falls back to the small, safe grid-convergence correction. The near-symmetric-alias and 45°-refusal cases are pinned deterministically by 3 new unit tests; the real-deed/real-parcel click-through is the live piece owed below.
- **What was shipped (B625):** the deed plotter drew bearings as **true-north** azimuths, but TX surveys use **State Plane grid north** (~1.5–2° off near Houston → ~90–120 ft over a long line), so a plotted deed landed rotated off the true-north county parcel. New `lib/deedAlign.js` solves the **rigid** rotation+translation to overlay the deed on the held parcel (scale locked — deed dimensions preserved; holes move as one group); a one-click **"Align to parcel"** banner + panel button + a manual Rotate° stepper apply it and report the rotation + fit residual honestly.
- **✅ Proven here (headless, logged-out):** the full select → Align → snap flow lands the boundary on the parcel to sub-foot residual and moves the save-and-except hole with it (harness above). The math (rigid fit recovers a known rotation; grid convergence = ~+1.5° at Katy, sign cross-checked vs the EPSG:2278 projection) is unit-tested.
- **✅ Ran the fix on the REAL Grand Port data** (pulled read-only from `sites` in `planyr_production` via the Supabase MCP — site `smqfy2r7pdec`, Chambers County, origin 29.807/−94.877): grid convergence here is **2.01°** (confirms the basis-of-bearings diagnosis). Fitting the real **"Tract 1 – 94.53 Acres"** deed (95.4 ac, 45 pts) to the loaded county parcel gives a best rotation of **4.06°** but a **221 ft (10.6%) residual → flagged NOT confident** — because the county parcel is **100.56 ac and a materially different shape** (it extends ~858 ft further **east** than the deed; they share only the west edge). So the tool behaves correctly (rotates to best fit, honestly flags "loose — verify") but the real misalignment is **partly rotation, partly that the loaded GIS outline isn't the same polygon as the deed** (parent/adjacent tract, or the wrong lot selected). **Separately:** the **"94.91 acres"** plot is a **0.38 ac / 119 ft-wide sliver** — a bad metes-and-bounds *parse* of that description (see B626), not an alignment problem.
- **Why the in-app click-through still pends:** confirming the *button + banner + snap animation* in the running UI on the real project needs the signed-in browser + live GIS the sandbox can't reach (see V194). The geometry/outcome is already proven above.

### V194 — B613 + B634 (the fix; commit/PR + in-code/test labels keep the provisional B630): a Fort Bend parcel click/search must NOT flash the "statewide backup" notice when FBCAD is healthy ❌ FAIL found live 2026-07-03 (false notice on EVERY FB click) → 🔧 root-caused + fix shipped (B630 label + B643 eager-race) → ⏳ live re-verify owed (sandbox Chromium egress resets all GIS hosts, so the click-through can't run here)
- **Added** 2026-07-02 · **Cadence** once (fix acceptance) · **Last checked** 2026-07-03 (Cowork, signed in on planyr.io — **FAILED**, see below; then B630 fix: lint 0 · **2281 tests green** incl. 6 new `isStatewideBackup` cases · build green) · **Next check** — on planyr.io, in a real browser, confirm the false notice is GONE (no sign-in needed — the parcel layer is public/anonymous).
- **❌ What the live run found (Cowork, 2026-07-03):** on the live signed-in map, **3 independent Fort Bend clicks all showed the amber "Statewide backup — Fort Bend county's server is unavailable; shown from TxGIO" notice** — including a plain residential rooftop. Decisive evidence it was a code bug, not FBCAD being down: a direct in-page `fetch()` of the FBCAD Esri endpoint for the exact clicked point returned **HTTP 200, featureCount = 1** with the full FBCAD schema, and the network tab showed **the app itself calling that same FBCAD URL and getting 200 on every click** — so FBCAD's primary was up and answering, yet the app labeled it unavailable.
- **🔧 Root cause (B630) — NOT the circuit breaker (the live report's hypothesis was close but off).** The breaker correctly ignores "200 + 0 features" (B245), and it was CLOSED (FBCAD was being queried, per the 200s). The real culprit: the click path (`identifyParcelEager`) races the county CAD and the statewide TxGIO layer **in parallel and takes the first to answer** — and FBCAD's Esri layer is a hair slower than TxGIO's identify, so **TxGIO kept WINNING THE RACE**. The old `viaBackup = STATEWIDE_KEYS.includes(hit.county) && realPrimaries.length > 0` then read "the statewide source answered" as "the county server is down" — a false alarm on every healthy click.
- **✅ Fix shipped (B630, this branch):** new pure `isStatewideBackup()` in `lib/sourceHealth.js` — a statewide answer is flagged a "backup" **only when the county's own CAD was genuinely unavailable this click** (its breaker was open → it was dropped from the query), never when a healthy CAD was queried but merely lost the parallel race. Wired into both the map-click (`handleClick`) and the search-select (`selectParcelAt`) paths in `MapFinder.jsx`. Proven here: lint 0 · full suite **2281 green** (incl. 6 new B630 cases: race-lost ⇒ no notice, breaker-open ⇒ real backup, statewide-only area, border straddle) · build green.
- **🔧 Follow-on fix (B643, this branch) — the eager RACE itself, so FBCAD's OWN data shows (V194 step 3):** B630 made the *notice* honest, but TxGIO still won the parallel race, so a Fort Bend click could select TxGIO's coarser copy (missing FBCAD's appraisal values). B643 tags identify candidates with `statewide` and has `identifyParcelEager` (`lib/arcgis.js`) **prefer a healthy real CAD** — a real-CAD hit resolves immediately; a statewide hit waits a bounded ~1.2s `BACKUP_GRACE_MS` for an in-flight CAD before being accepted — so a healthy FBCAD wins the race and its own parcel/appraisal data shows, while a genuinely-hung CAD still can't stall the click past the grace (the B244 eager guarantee holds). With the CAD winning, `hit.county` is the CAD (not statewide), so `isStatewideBackup` is doubly false. Proven here: lint 0 · **2429 tests green** (post `origin/main` merge; incl. my 3 new eager-preference/grace cases in `test/arcgis.test.js`) · build green. If a healthy FBCAD still loses the race in the field, the grace is a one-line tune.
- **⏳ Why the live re-verify still pends (not auth — a sandbox egress limit):** this sandbox's Chromium **resets every external GIS host** (`services2.arcgis.com`, `feature.geographic.texas.gov` → `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`; curl through the agent proxy reaches them fine, so it's a browser-egress gap, not the code). `gis-verify/fbcad-hosted-primary-verify.mjs` is ready to run the moment a browser can reach the host.
- **⏳ Steps on planyr.io (any teammate with an unrestricted browser — NOT Michael's job):**
  1. Open the Site Planner over **Fort Bend County** (Sugar Land / Katy / Richmond area). Click **Select parcels**, zoom to ~street level → confirm parcel **outlines paint** promptly.
  2. **Click several Fort Bend lots** (incl. a residential rooftop) → each selects, and the on-canvas amber **"statewide backup…"** notice does **NOT** appear (this is the B630 regression — it must be gone now that FBCAD answering, or merely losing the race, no longer trips the "unavailable" flag).
  3. Confirm the selected lot's **Appraisal data** shows owner, situs, values (Land/Improvement/Total), acreage, legal, land use.
  4. In the planner's **Add parcel → Identify from county GIS**, search a Fort Bend **account (R-number / QuickRef ID)** and a **site address** → both return the right lot with no false backup notice.
  5. Sanity: Harris and Chambers parcels still work unchanged; and if FBCAD is ever *genuinely* down (force it / its breaker opens), a click SHOULD still fall back to TxGIO **with** the honest backup notice.

### V191 — B610: a Drive file whose key↔id mapping write FAILS reports an honest failure (not "saved ✓") and leaves no orphaned Drive copy ⏳ needs a signed-in browser + a forced mapping-write failure (Cowork 2026-07-03: NOT run — would break Drive saves on production; needs a staging Supabase)
- **Added** 2026-07-02 · **Cadence** once (bug-fix acceptance) · **Last checked** 2026-07-03 (**Cowork — deliberately NOT run on production**, see below · earlier: lint 0 · 2163 tests green · build green) · **Next check** — on a **branch/staging Supabase** where the `drive_files` INSERT policy can be revoked + restored safely, signed in.
- **⏳ Cowork attempt 2026-07-03 — deliberately NOT run:** forcing the `public.drive_files` write to fail on the *production* Supabase (revoking its INSERT policy / renaming the table) is a live access-control mutation that would break Drive saves mid-session — out of bounds and risky on production. Verify on a **branch/staging Supabase** where the policy can be toggled and restored safely.

If the `public.drive_files` write fails **after** the Drive bytes already landed, `adapter.save` rolls the bytes back (`backend.remove`) and returns a visible failure; the upload COMMIT deletes the Drive file and returns 502. Previously the upload reported success and the drawing went silently missing on next open. Can't be verified here — the whole path is auth-gated (Supabase session) + Drive-backed, and a mapping-write failure has to be induced. *(B409-rework note, 2026-07-11: the commit guard now lives in `functions/api/uploads/[id]/complete.js` — the old `/api/files/resumable` route was retired; the guard itself is unchanged and unit-covered in `test/uploadEndpoints.test.js`.)*

  1. Sign in. Temporarily force the mapping write to fail — e.g. in Supabase, revoke the INSERT policy on `public.drive_files` (or rename the table) so the `drive_files` upsert returns 4xx/5xx.
  2. In the Library (or Review), drop/file a PDF into a project. Confirm the save badge/queue shows an **honest failure** (not "saved ✓", not a silent green) — never a phantom success. (Since the B409 rework there is no Supabase upload fallback: the row must read FAILED with a retryable error.)
  3. In Google Drive, confirm **no orphaned copy** of that file was left behind (the rollback deleted it).
  4. Restore the `drive_files` policy; re-file the same PDF; confirm it saves and a reload opens the drawing (mapping resolved).

### V167 — B551: Stitcher releases pointer capture on a mid-pan blur (no frozen grab cursor) ✅ unit/anti-drift here; ⏳ runtime check owed (Cowork 2026-07-03: NOT reproducible via automation — needs a real mid-gesture window-blur)

### V134 — B459: cloud-save content guard (never silently overwrite a fuller row with a thin one) ✅ 9 unit tests (`wouldThinClobber`) + lint 0 + 1504 tests + build green; ⏳ one signed-in stale-tab clobber repro (Cowork, Phase B)
- **What changed.** The cloud save's compare-and-swap checks only the version NUMBER, not content — so a stale/thin tab at a matching version could overwrite a fuller cloud row (the 8 South 5-building loss). Now the save remembers the content baseline it last synced and BLOCKS a push that would drop ≥2 items the cloud still has with no delete-tombstone, surfacing the B455 loud+blocking conflict instead of clobbering (the cloud stays intact → reload union-merges it back). (`cloudSync.js` `wouldThinClobber` + `siteContent`/`siteTombs`.)
- **Verified (sandbox).** Pure decision unit-tested deterministically (`test/cloudThinGuard.test.js`, 9 cases): the 5-building clobber blocks; a single undo passes; a tombstoned bulk delete passes; partial-tombstone and boundary (lost-2 vs lost-1) cases; cross-collection counting.
- **Why ⏳ (Cowork, signed-in — NOT markable from the sandbox).** Reproduce the real clobber: sign in, open a plan with N buildings in two tabs (or force a stale/thin tab), have the stale tab attempt a save → expect it BLOCKED with the "saving paused — reload to merge" banner and the cloud row UNCHANGED (still N buildings); reload → all N restored. The logged-out sandbox can't drive auth or the cloud. Part of Phase B.

### V122 — Live PK is single-column `id`; docs corrected + degrade-branch upserts repointed (B280 follow-up) ✅ cloud-save round-trip VERIFIED LIVE (Cowork 2026-06-25); ⏳ only the version-LESS-DB fallback branch stays dormant/untested (latent-path hardening)
- **✅ 2026-06-25 (Cowork, signed-in on planyr.io):** an edit (drew + deleted a markup in a Review) **autosaved and the header read "Cloud sync: Synced"** — the primary `casUpsert` (keyed on `id`) round-trip works live. The version-LESS-DB id-first fallback stays dormant on production (the `version` column exists there), so that branch is still untested — low-priority latent-path hardening, not a user-facing gap.
- **What changed.** A Cowork session with live-DB access confirmed (via `pg_constraint`) that
  `public.sites` AND `public.doc_reviews` have **`PRIMARY KEY (id)`** on planyr-production — NOT the
  `(user_id, id)` the docs claimed. That drift had already been migrated in by `db/team_sharing.sql`
  (PK `(user_id,id)→(id)` so one row per project survives a teammate edit); `user_id` stays the
  owner column + RLS predicate. Fixed three things: (1) the two `CLAUDE.md` "Table schema" blocks
  now say `primary key (id)` with a note; (2) the **degrade-branch** plain-upserts in `cloudSync.js`
  (`sites`) and `reviewStore.js` (`doc_reviews`) were keyed on `onConflict:"user_id,id"` alone —
  which 42P10s on the live single-column PK — now they try `"id"` first and fall back to
  `"user_id,id"` only for a genuinely pre-migration DB, mirroring `upsertFileFacts`' existing pattern;
  (3) the B280 seed (`e2e/seed/seed.sql`) was already made constraint-independent.
- **Why ⏳.** The degrade branch only fires when the `version` column is absent; on production the
  column exists, so the fixed path is dormant there (the primary `casUpsert` already keys on `id`).
  The seed itself is ✅ confirmed live. The owed check is one signed-in save against a DB lacking the
  `version` column, to watch the new id-first fallback succeed — low priority (latent-path hardening).
- **Steps / Expect.** Sign in → edit a site → Save shows "Saved" (cloud write ok). On a version-less
  DB the network call upserts with `onConflict=id` and does not 42P10. Cadence: once. Last checked: —.

This corroborates the 2026-06-23 SQL-editor check via a second access path. Also confirmed the `CLAUDE.md` PK-block fix is live in `main`. **Still ⏳ (unchanged):** the low-priority version-less-DB id-first fallback round-trip (dormant on prod, which has the `version` column).

### V13 — ★ Persistence: saved work must never disappear (B124 / B125) — durability ✅ / resume-into-planner: ❌ confirmed 2026-06-25 → **FIX SHIPPED same session (B478)**, signed-in confirm owed — HIGH PRIORITY
- **Added** 2026-06-16 · **Cadence** once (data-safety acceptance) + on-change · **Last checked** 2026-06-25 (Cowork re-confirmed ❌; fix then shipped — see below) · **Next check** the signed-in resume confirm (now **V143**)
- **❌ RE-CONFIRMED 2026-06-25 (Cowork, signed-in on planyr.io), then ROOT-CAUSE PINNED + FIXED the same session.** Cowork opened **8 South** (URL `#/project/smqiljx5fngg/site`, planner rendered), ran `location.reload()` → at both ~2 s and ~7 s the app **bounced to the finder**, breadcrumb "Select a project", URL **stripped to `#/`**; a cold navigate straight to a project URL likewise bounced. Data durability is fine (8 South stays intact + reopenable) — it's purely the resume UX.
- **✅ FIX SHIPPED this session (B478, branch `claude/v13-resume-into-planner`).** ROOT CAUSE found in `SitePlannerApp.jsx`: on a **signed-in** deep link/refresh the user's cloud sites aren't in the local store at the first synchronous render (auth + `pullCloud` are async), so `activeSiteId` is momentarily null even though the route names a project. Two boot reactions then destroyed the resume **before** the pull could finish: (1) the active-project→URL sync wrote that transient `null` over the route, **stripping `#/project/<id>/site` → `#/`** (and bouncing to the finder); (2) the "tidy a dangling `currentSite`" cleanup **nulled the pointer** because the cloud site only *looked* absent. FIX: a `bootResolved` gate (pure `lib/bootResume.js`) holds BOTH reconciliations until the first auth + pull settles; the resume target is now one shared, unit-tested `pickResumeTarget`. Verified: lint 0 · **1585 tests (+11 `bootResume.test.js`)** · build green · logged-out headless **8/8** (`ui-audit/verify-resume-into-planner.mjs` — deep-link + reload stays in the planner, route intact, pointer preserved) + `verify-new-site-save.mjs` **10/10** (no regression). **The signed-in async-gap repro can't run in the sandbox (no Supabase → no gap), so the signed-in confirm is owed — tracked as V143 below.**
- **2026-06-20 (Cowork — real signed-in Chrome on planyr.io, cloud ON; deployed bundle SitePlannerApp-BuRTao7i.js, Supabase HTTP 200 each boot, no console errors):**
  - **✅ Data durability (the critical part):** drew 3 buildings on a signed-in throwaway site; "Synced ✓"; the site + every element survived **~6 reloads** and reopened intact from the finder. Work never disappeared on its own.
  - **❌ Resume-into-planner (step 2):** every reload — **soft (F5) AND hard (Ctrl+Shift+R)**, on a brand-new site AND an established/reopened site — lands on the **map/finder**, NOT the open planner. Confirmed at the storage layer: `currentSite:v1` holds the open site's id going *into* the reload, and boot **nulls it** and shows the finder; even force-setting `currentSite:v1` in localStorage then reloading still nulled it → finder. No crash, no data loss — but it contradicts the written "resume straight into the planner, NOT bounced to the map" expectation. (Matches the prior "reload bounces NEW sites to finder" note, but now reproduces for established sites too.)
  - Steps 4 (DevTools offline) & 5 (signed-out→sign-in bridge) not run: the offline toggle isn't drivable via the browser tools, and re-sign-in requires a password Cowork won't enter. Worth a manual pass.
- **Why this matters:** this is the fix for the owner-reported data-loss scare — work vanishing on its
  own a couple minutes after a reload. Root cause: `pullCloud` rebuilt the local cache from the cloud
  list **alone** and silently dropped any not-yet-synced local site; the resume then couldn't find the
  open site and bounced to the map. Confirm in a real browser that saved work is now durable.
- **Steps (signed in, on planyr.io):**
  1. Sign in. Open or create a site, add a **building**; wait for the header badge to read **"Synced ✓"**.
  2. **Reload** → you **resume straight into the planner** on that site (NOT bounced to the map) and the
     building is still there.
  3. **Switch to another browser tab for ~2–3 minutes, then return** (refocus the Planyr tab) → the site
     + building must **still be there** and you are **not** bounced to the map. (This is the exact
     "disappears on its own" trigger — a background re-sign-in event firing the cloud re-pull.)
  4. **Forced not-yet-synced repro (DevTools):** Network tab → **Offline**. Add another building → a
     **loud red banner** ("your last change didn't reach the cloud … **Retry now**") appears and the badge
     reads Offline/Unsaved. **Reload while still offline** → the building is **still there** (not dropped).
     Go back **Online** → it syncs (badge → "Synced ✓") and the red banner clears.
  5. **On-device → account bridge:** while **signed out**, create a site (saved on this device only).
     **Sign in** → a blue banner "You have N site(s) saved on **this device** that aren't in your account
     yet" appears; click **"Bring them into my account"** → the site joins the account list and the banner
     clears. The signed-out copy is **kept** (non-destructive).

### V19 — Site element labels: no overlap pile; level-of-detail on zoom-out (B121 increment 1) ❌→FIX SHIPPED 2026-07-22 (B951 — parcel-area badges now collision obstacles); ⏳ live re-confirm on Bain owed
- **❌ 2026-07-22 (Cowork round 5, signed-in on planyr.io, Bain — Fort Bend, Concept A) — REPRODUCED TWICE, then FIXED same session (B951).** At a zoom where the building cluster + a nearby detention pond + a small parcel fit together, "Building 4"'s label stack (166,240 sf / incl. 2 bump-outs / 260′ × 614′) overprinted an adjacent parcel-area badge ("5.24 ac") — reading as garbled "166,240 sf ac". Root cause: the label-collision engine only pooled ELEMENT labels; the parcel-area acreage chips were a SEPARATE fixed layer it never saw. **B951 fix:** `layoutLabels` now takes an `opts.obstacles` list and the Site Planner seeds each visible parcel-area chip's box as an immovable obstacle, so an element label (and the red dim ticks) yield around a badge instead of overprinting. Unit-tested (`test/labelLayout.test.js` B951 suite) + build green.
- **✅ Headless re-verified on the REAL canvas this session (logged-out, `vite preview`, ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK).** Drew a parcel (its "35.64 ac" acreage badge renders at the centroid) + a building. (1) **Coincident case** — building centred ON the badge: the building's name/sf/dims label YIELDS (hidden) and the "35.64 ac" badge renders clean and un-garbled (before the fix the label "Building 1 / … sf / … × …" would have piled onto the badge — the reported garble). (2) **Offset case** — building beside the badge: the full label "Building 1 / 163,573 sf / 522′ × 313′" renders AND does NOT overlap the badge (proving labels aren't universally suppressed — they only yield around the badge). The red "313′" dim tick also clears the badge. Zero page errors. Screenshots in `scratchpad/b949-parcel-building.png`.
- **⏳ Live re-confirm owed (SIGNED IN, Bain — nice-to-have):** the mechanism is now proven on the real canvas above; the ORIGINAL repro cited Bain's real parcels + aerial at a specific zoom (a zoom-/data-density LIVE-VERIFY class), so a Cowork confirm on Bain at that exact scene (building cluster + the "5.24 ac" badge near Building 4, across a zoom-out/in round trip) closes it fully. Tracked under **B951**.
- **Added** 2026-06-16 · **Cadence** once (feature acceptance) · **Last checked** 2026-07-22 (❌ reproduced → B951 fix shipped) · **Next check** the Bain re-confirm above
- **Steps:** Open a site and lay out adjacent elements (a big building, a narrow trailer strip beside it,
  a detention pond, a couple of sidewalks). (1) **Zoomed in:** each element shows its full centred label
  (name + sf/count + dimensions) as before. (2) **Zoom out:** labels should *thin out*, not pile up — the
  dimensions line drops first, then the area line, leaving the name; the **narrow trailer strip** should
  drop to just its name (or hide) rather than spilling a 3-line label past its ~50′ width. (3) **Crowd
  test:** push several labelled elements close together and confirm their centred labels no longer
  overprint into an unreadable stack — a lower-priority label yields (shrinks or disappears) to the
  bigger / building label rather than stacking on top. Zoom back in → the hidden labels return.
- **Expect:** no two centred element-name labels overprint at any zoom; buildings / bigger elements keep
  their labels; nothing crashes; non-labelled elements (paving / parking / roads) are unaffected.
- **Known-not-yet (increment 2 — do NOT fail for these):** the **red edge-dimension ticks** ("300′",
  "638′") are still a separate layer and may overlap the centred names; no leader lines yet. Tracked under B121.
- **If it fails:** not critical (no data risk) — log ❌ here with what looked wrong (especially a label
